data.content_ref: inline:The target's proposed evidence — showing the panel applies checklist criteria with higher fidelity on divergence cases — cannot, within a single evaluation, distinguish genuine rule-mediated reliability from a panel that has simply memorized the checklist's surface heuristics for the specific case types in that evaluation. 'Higher fidelity application' on divergence cases is observationally indistinguishable from pattern-matching to checklist cues that correlate with, but do not constitute, genuine evidentiary reasoning. The target's own mechanism acknowledges that 'surface features correlate with easy cases,' but its proposed remedy (checking whether errors shift from intuition-type to rule-type) does not resolve the problem: a 'rule-type' error pattern can emerge from rote application of checklist heuristics without any understanding of the evidentiary weights the checklist prescribes. Within a single evaluation there is no held-out transfer test to show the panel is applying the checklist's logic rather than exploiting evaluation-specific regularities, so the distinguishing evidence the target names is not actually available under the single-evaluation constraint the problem imposes.
